newsitem.title: UK: IFC sets longest maturity rand Eurobond at 10 yrs.
newsitem.headline: IFC sets longest maturity rand Eurobond at 10 yrs.

text.p: The World Bank's private sector financing arm, the International Finance Corp, on Thursday launched the longest-dated Eurorand bond, which is also the first ever zero-coupon Eurorand issue.
Gerry Moes, syndicate manager at lead manager Hambros Bank, a regular underwriter in the Eurorand sector, said it was a ground-breaking transaction.
The 500 million rand zero-coupon 10-year bond yields just over 14.0 percent.
Another syndicate manager at a German bank said the deal offered certain investors tax advantages and praised the deal.
"Its a new twist in a burgeoning market and an interesting development," he said.
Added to this, Moes said Hambros had a lot of experience in the Australian and New Zealand dollar zero-coupon markets.
"With a high coupon market a zero-coupon deal makes a lot of sense," he said. "It has a very attractive cash price."
He said with the renewed confidence in the currency and domestic bond markets it offered a good opportunity.
"We started with 400 million rand and were in a position to increase the deal," he said.
The deal was syndicated between 14 banks and sales were focused in Benelux, Italy, Germany, Switzerland as well as the Far East.

A zero coupon bond pays no coupon but is issued at a deep discount to face value. The difference between the issue and redemption prices creates a hefty capital gain which boosts the yield close to market levels.
